newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar tightly mixed, switches active.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar tightly mixed, switches active.

text.p: White sugar futures lost their grip on the firmness seen earlier in the session but switch trades were the order of the day as the further forwards attracted more interest, traders said.
"The (March/May) spread is remaining steady but it's the quietest day of the week, the majority of March is on a switch basis," said one trader.
"It's a mixture of nothing," he said, noting trade interest to buy August/October from broker sellers.
But values were content to meander rangebound in relatively modest volume after the heavy AA-dominated trade earlier in the week.
At 1645 GMT March stood 20 cents firmer at $304.50 while May was up 10 cents at $301.90. Overall turnover amounted to 1,906 lots, including some 500 lots in against actuals trades.
Traders reported little business on the March whites premium, which widened out to around $70 as persisent producer raws selling outpaced the firmness in London.
The premium was still trapped in the tight range seen over the week, with buyers noted at $68.50 and sellers waiting in the wings at $70 and above.

Physical news was thin on the ground although Iran is expected to be in the market next week to buy 14,000 tonnes of white sugar for April shipment after cancelling its tender this week due to higher world prices.
In Paris values were also tightly mixed and Matif volume was on the light side at just 161 lots.
March was up 20 cents at $303.70 and May down 30 cents at $301.20.
